prompt:
Architecture work item for the Alder Biologics virtualization estate. The three products in `estate-inventory.json` must move to the VCF 9.0.2 operations stack without treating management-domain and workload-domain placement as the whole design. Implement `MigrationPlanClient.java` as a single-file, plain-JDK Java client that reads the inventory and `compatibility-snapshot.json` and writes `migration-plan.json` in the exact `migration-plan.schema.json` shape. Its command line is `java MigrationPlanClient.java estate-inventory.json compatibility-snapshot.json migration-plan.json`.

The output is the architecture artifact, not an essay. It must map every inventoried source product and exact version to its target component; give concrete site, domain, cluster, and failure-domain placement and appliance sizing for VCF Operations, VCF Automation, VCF Operations for Logs, Fleet Management, and the workload collectors; account once for every inventoried content and configuration item as carry, recreate, replace, or abandon; state the applicable end-of-general-support boundary for every source; and provide the required migration steps in order. Every step needs its technical entry and exit gates and must name the source product and version and target components it affects.

Before finalizing the client, research current Broadcom-published material for supported migration paths, content compatibility, sizing, and support boundaries. Record the Broadcom pages you consulted under `research.sourcesConsulted`, with title, URL, access date, and the claims used.

Run `java TestMain.java`. Do not modify `TestMain.java`, the schema, inventory, compatibility snapshot, or `.gitignore`; complete the work in `MigrationPlanClient.java` only.
